ar_nomar_wall.blurb: Nomar Wall is one of the walls on the north side of Stack Rock, a remote cliff in the Richland Creek area of north-central Arkansas. Eight routes are split evenly between sport and trad, running from one 5.7 through several 5.10s to a few at 5.11. The cliff as a whole curves around in a crown shape, so parts of it take sun or shade at different times of day, and its steeper sections stay dry in light rain. Reaching the cliff takes around twenty minutes on foot, and loose rock turns up here and there on the rock.

ar_cowboy_boulder.blurb: Cowboy Boulder is a freestanding block in the Fern climbing area of northwest Arkansas, a small creek-side zone where most climbs stay under fifty feet. It has seven lines: six bolted sport routes and one boulder problem at the easy end. The sport routes begin around 5.6, with a few at 5.10 and two up at 5.12, so it suits someone wanting a short session on short, varied lines rather than a long day. It sits close to a second bolted boulder, so the two are easy to combine.
ar_cowboy_boulder.approach: Follow the PK Boulder trail west from the parking area and cross the stream, then turn south. The first of two boulders with bolts is Small Wall Boulder, and the second is Cowboy Boulder.

ar_hillside_boulder_area.blurb: Hillside Boulder Area is a small bouldering spot in Riverside Park, a couple of miles outside Searcy in northeast Arkansas. It sits right at the start of the trail, just below the lot beside the playground, and you scramble down one of several ways to reach the base. Five boulder problems run from about V1 to V5, and two top-rope lines are rated around 5.10. The surrounding Riverside crag is described as a modest cluster of problems with a few good ones among them.

ar_scr_house.blurb: SCR House is a bouldering sector within the Gasfields, near Little Rock, Arkansas. It has seven problems, from easy V1s up through a pair of mid-grade lines to a few hard ones, with the top end reaching V12. The climbing has a cave with a crack system, a steep overhanging start and a traverse, with jugs, thin crimps and slopers on the holds, plus a water groove. One line is noted as always wet or dirty, and another is marked as chossy.
ar_scr_house.parking_note: Space to leave a car is very limited here, so pull off the main dirt road rather than blocking it.

ar_1_prow_d_wall.blurb: Prow'd Wall is the first section of Capitol Crag, in the Crystal Bluff area of the River Valley near Little Rock. The face is orange stone with a prominent arete on its left side. Seven routes, six bolted and one trad, give a friendly spread: a 5.6, a 5.7 and a 5.8, three at 5.9, and a single 5.10. The crag as a whole is sunny for most of the day with shade early in the morning, and some parts sit under trees. Some routes at the crag run past a hundred feet, so check rope length.
ar_1_prow_d_wall.approach: Take the main trail to the fork and go right, then cross the gully. The wall is marked by a prominent shield of orange rock high above, and it is the first one reached at the crag.

ar_tang_boulder.blurb: Tang Boulder is in the North Forty at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas. Seven problems range from V1 up to V10, with a gap in the middle and plenty of choice both below V3 and in the V7 to V10 range. The south face takes sun, although the overhang throws some shade. An obvious vertical crack runs up the middle. The hill leading up to it is steep, and you reach it by following the base trail north of the bathrooms and past another boulder, with Tang up the slope to the left.
